newsitem.title: USA: U.S., Brazil form group to resolve trade flap.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Brazil form group to resolve trade flap.

text.p: Brazil's trade minister criticized U.S. barriers on some Brazilian imports on Monday and said the countries had set up a group to resolve the dispute.
Francisco Dornelles, Brazil's minister of industry, commerce and tourism, said U.S. and European Union import restrictions were costing Brazil between $4 billion and $5 billion a year.

"The restrictions that you have in the United States on Brazilian exports are much higher than there are in Brazil to exports from any other country," he said in an address to the Brazilian-American Chamber of Commerce.

Dornelles said he met on Monday with Commerce Secretary William Daley and Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman to discuss limits and quotas for Brazilian imports. They include steel, ferrous alloys, sugar and tobacco.
Brazil and the United States agreed to set up a technical group to study the issue. It should begin work in 15 to 20 days in Brasilia.
The United States is "very interested, as Brazil is, in solving all these points, to erase all the difficulties which exist," he told reporters after his speech.
Dornelles added that, by mid-April, Brazil and Argentina would resolve disputes over trade that include differences over automobile imports.
"I'm very optimistic about our relationship with Argentina and I believe that the small points we still have (in dispute) ...will be solved by the middle of April," he said.
Asked about Brazil's growing trade deficit, Dornelles said the reformist government moved to boost exports by eliminating taxes and extending credit and insurance guarantees to companies.
Brazil did not need to devalue its currency, the real, to make exports cheaper and thus more attractive, he said.
Brazil's trade deficit for the first two weeks of March totaled $456 million. The gap for the first two months of 1997 was $2 billion.
